key_insight: DermDepth shows that single-view dermatology images can be reconstructed into metric-scale 3D surfaces without extra hardware or multiple captures.
clinical_relevance: This could improve lesion and wound measurement, morphology tracking, and size assessment in dermatology and skin cancer screening using standard cameras.
method: Trained a monocular 3D reconstruction model on D-Synth, a synthetic dermoscopic dataset with pixel-perfect 3D labels.
Used real dermoscopic and macroscopic benchmarks to evaluate metric scale, geometry, and surface-normal texture quality.
Fine-tuned on a small set of clinical samples to improve transfer across diverse skin tones, wounds, and lesion sizes.
evidence_signal: According to the abstract, training on D-Synth reduced metric scale error from over 16× to under 1.1× on real dermoscopic data and generalized across three real-world benchmarks spanning millimeters to hundreds of centimeters.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on careful real-world fine-tuning and validation across device types, skin tones, and lesion/wound appearance before clinical use.
paper_title: DermDepth: Toward Monocular Metric Scale 3D Reconstruction Models for Dermatology
